I’d make *The Department of Unlikely Incidents*: a series of short films disguised as cheerful old workplace-safety videos. They teach you what to do if your shadow quits, the moon gets stuck in a chimney, or gravity moves one floor up. Shot with handmade miniatures, stiff diagrams, and relentlessly soothing narration. Each film’s instructions contradict the last, while the narrator insists the situation is routine.

The fun is in treating cosmic nonsense with bureaucratic seriousness: the world can come apart, but someone still has to fill out the form. I’d want it funny first, then gradually unsettling—not another haunted room, but a whole civilization trying to manage the impossible with laminated procedures.
